## Accessors

<MemberHeading id="currenttime" depth="3" name="currentTime" sig="get currentTime(): number" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L179" sourceLabel="playback.ts:179" />

Elapsed animation time in milliseconds within the current iteration, always clamped to `[0, duration]` (§11.1).

<MemberHeading id="directionmode" depth="3" name="directionMode" sig="get directionMode(): PlaybackDirectionMode" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L201" sourceLabel="playback.ts:201" />

The authored direction mode (§13).

<MemberHeading id="finished" depth="3" name="finished" sig="get finished(): Promise<PlaybackResult>" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L191" sourceLabel="playback.ts:191" />

The completion promise of the current run (§11.1). It resolves with `{ status: "finished" }` when all iterations complete naturally, or `{ status: "cancelled" }` on ordinary cancellation — never a rejection. Each run started by `play()` gets its own promise; awaiting this getter before any run settles waits for the next settlement of whatever run is current when read.

<MemberHeading id="iterationcount" depth="3" name="iterationCount" sig="get iterationCount(): number" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L211" sourceLabel="playback.ts:211" />

The completed iterations of the current run (§13).

<MemberHeading id="iterations" depth="3" name="iterations" sig="get iterations(): number | 'infinite'" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L196" sourceLabel="playback.ts:196" />

Configured total iterations, including the initial one (§13).

<MemberHeading id="playbackrate" depth="3" name="playbackRate" sig="get playbackRate(): number" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L221" sourceLabel="playback.ts:221" />

The playback rate multiplier (§11.1, §16). Any finite number is accepted: `2` plays twice as fast, `-1` runs backwards, `0` holds time. Changing the rate never jumps animation time — only future elapsed-time deltas are scaled relative to the current timestamp (§12, §16).

<MemberHeading id="reversed" depth="3" name="reversed" sig="get reversed(): boolean" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L206" sourceLabel="playback.ts:206" />

Whether the current iteration runs backwards, after any `reverse()` calls.

<MemberHeading id="state" depth="3" name="state" sig="get state(): PlaybackState" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L171" sourceLabel="playback.ts:171" />

The current lifecycle state (§12).

## Methods

<MemberHeading id="cancel" depth="3" name="cancel" sig="cancel(): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L350" sourceLabel="playback.ts:350" />

Stops playback and resolves the run's promise with `{ status: "cancelled" }` (§12). The last rendered transform is retained — cancellation does not attempt to restore an unknown original target transform. Cancellation and natural completion are separate outcomes; a finished or already-cancelled instance ignores this call.

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="dispose" depth="3" name="dispose" sig="dispose(): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L367" sourceLabel="playback.ts:367" />

Permanently releases playback resources (§12): unregisters from the engine, releases target ownership, invokes the adapter's optional `dispose` cleanup hook (§17.1) — never destroying the underlying DOM element, canvas context, or graphics resource (Appendix B.8) — and settles any pending `finished` promise as cancelled so awaiting code cannot hang. Idempotent; every other operation on a disposed instance throws (§12).

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="onengineupdate" depth="3" name="onEngineUpdate" sig="onEngineUpdate(timeMs: number): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L389" sourceLabel="playback.ts:389" />

Called by the `PlaybackEngine` with the current clock timestamp. Advances time by the elapsed wall-clock delta scaled by `playbackRate` and the iteration direction — timestamp-based, never frame-count-based (§16).

**Parameters**

- `timeMs` (number)

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="pause" depth="3" name="pause" sig="pause(): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L297" sourceLabel="playback.ts:297" />

Stops time advancement while retaining playback state and time (§12). A later `play()` resumes from the retained time. No-op unless running.

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="play" depth="3" name="play" sig="play(): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L251" sourceLabel="playback.ts:251" />

Starts or resumes playback (§12). Resuming a paused instance continues at the retained time; starting from `idle`, `finished`, or `cancelled` begins a new run from the beginning of the timeline in the current direction (§12) with its own `Playback.finished` promise. Starting (or resuming) takes target ownership, superseding any other playback on the same target (§14).

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="reverse" depth="3" name="reverse" sig="reverse(): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L310" sourceLabel="playback.ts:310" />

Changes playback direction (§12, §13). Time is retained and continues in the new direction from wherever it currently sits. The changed direction is also the direction a restarted run uses — `play()` after finishing restarts "in current direction" (§12).

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="seek" depth="3" name="seek" sig="seek(timeMs: number): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L321" sourceLabel="playback.ts:321" />

Sets elapsed animation time within the current iteration, in milliseconds (§12). Out-of-range times clamp to `[0, duration]`. Seeking immediately re-evaluates and submits the transform to the target when one is attached, without changing playback state.

**Parameters**

- `timeMs` (number)

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="seekprogress" depth="3" name="seekProgress" sig="seekProgress(progress: number): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L335" sourceLabel="playback.ts:335" />

Sets normalized animation progress in `[0, 1]` within the current iteration (§12), equivalent to `seek(progress × duration)`. Out-of-range progress clamps to the boundaries.

**Parameters**

- `progress` (number)

**Returns**

- `void`

# PlaybackDirectionMode
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/playbackdirectionmode/

<Signature code="PlaybackDirectionMode = 'normal' | 'reverse' | 'alternate' | 'alternate-reverse'" />

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/playback-ts/#L32" label="playback.ts:32" />

How playback direction behaves between iterations (§13). `alternate` and `alternate-reverse` flip direction every iteration; `normal` and `reverse` keep one direction for the whole run.

---

# PlaybackEngine
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/playbackengine/

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/playback/engine-ts/#L39" label="engine.ts:39" />

The centralized playback scheduler (§16). One engine drives all active playback instances: it reads the current time from its injectable `Clock`, steps every registered playback, and requests the next frame from its injectable `Scheduler` only while at least one playback is active — so there are no unnecessary updates when nothing is playing (§16). Animation time is timestamp-based, never frame-count-based: each update advances playbacks by the elapsed clock time scaled by their playback rate. Custom clocks and schedulers integrate without modifying the core (§21).

```ts
const engine = new PlaybackEngine({ clock: myClock, scheduler: myScheduler });
const playback = animation.attach(target, { engine });
playback.play(); // driven by `engine` instead of the shared default
```

---

# projectToCanvas2D
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/projecttocanvas2d/

<Signature
  code="projectToCanvas2D(
	matrix: Matrix4,
	options?: Canvas2DTargetOptions,
): readonly [number, number, number, number, number, number]"
/>

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/canvas-ts/#L66" label="canvas.ts:66" />

Projects a `Matrix4` into Canvas 2D's affine form (§17.3). Canvas 2D is an inherently 2D affine API: the required projection step maps the transformed homogeneous images of the origin and the X/Y basis vectors through perspective division (and the optional camera at `perspective` distance), then fits the 2D affine that reproduces those screen positions. For purely affine inputs this reduces exactly to their 2D affine part; for matrices with Z or perspective components it produces the projected result rather than silently forwarding a raw 4×4 matrix, which Canvas cannot represent.

**Parameters**

- `matrix` ([Matrix4](/keyframe-flow/docs/matrix4))
- `options` ([Canvas2DTargetOptions](/keyframe-flow/docs/canvas2dtargetoptions), optional)

**Returns**

- `readonly [number, number, number, number, number, number]`

**Example**

```ts
// +10 x at depth 50 with a camera at distance 100 projects to x = 20:
const [a, b, c, d, e, f] = projectToCanvas2D(m, { perspective: 100 });
ctx.setTransform(a, b, c, d, e, f); // e ≈ 20
```

---

# Quaternion
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/quaternion/

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/quaternion-ts/#L37" label="quaternion.ts:37" />

An immutable unit-friendly quaternion used as the library's internal rotation representation (§4.3). Components follow the Hamilton convention `(x, y, z, w)` with `w` as the scalar part.

Multiplication follows matrix conventions for column vectors: `a.multiply(b)` produces the rotation that applies `b` first and then `a`, mirroring `A × B` in §4.4.

**Example**

```ts
const turn = Quaternion.fromEuler(0, Math.PI / 2, 0); // yaw 90°, radians only
turn.rotateVector([1, 0, 0]); // Vector3 ≈ (0, 0, −1) — right-handed
```

---

  depth="3"
  name="constructor"
  sig="new Quaternion(
	x: number,
	y: number,
	z: number,
	w: number,
): Quaternion"
/>

**Parameters**

- `x` (number, default: `0`)
- `y` (number, default: `0`)
- `z` (number, default: `0`)
- `w` (number, default: `1`)

**Returns**

`Quaternion`

<MemberHeading id="rotatevector" depth="3" name="rotateVector" sig="rotateVector(v: Vector3Like): Vector3" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/quaternion-ts/#L184" sourceLabel="quaternion.ts:184" />

Rotates a vector by this quaternion: `v' = q · v · q*`.

**Parameters**

- `v` ([Vector3Like](/keyframe-flow/docs/vector3like))

- [`Vector3`](/keyframe-flow/docs/vector3)

<MemberHeading id="slerp" depth="3" name="slerp" sig="slerp(other: QuaternionObject, t: number): Quaternion" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/quaternion-ts/#L140" sourceLabel="quaternion.ts:140" />

Spherical linear interpolation toward `other` at parameter `t ∈ [0, 1]`.

Inputs are normalized before use and the shortest path on the 4D sphere is taken by default (§9.1). Endpoints reproduce the inputs exactly.

**Parameters**

- `other` ([QuaternionObject](/keyframe-flow/docs/quaternionobject))
- `t` (number)

**Returns**

- [`Quaternion`](/keyframe-flow/docs/quaternion)

<MemberHeading id="toarray" depth="3" name="toArray" sig="toArray(): [number, number, number, number]" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/quaternion-ts/#L251" sourceLabel="quaternion.ts:251" />

The `[x, y, z, w]` tuple form (Hamilton order).

**Returns**

- `[number, number, number, number]`

<MemberHeading id="toeuler" depth="3" name="toEuler" sig="toEuler(): readonly [number, number, number]" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/quaternion-ts/#L226" sourceLabel="quaternion.ts:226" />

Decomposes this rotation into Euler angles in radians, in the inverse of `Quaternion.fromEuler`'s intrinsic X → Y → Z convention (the angles whose `Rx · Ry · Rz` matrix reproduces this orientation). Angles are chosen by principal-value `asin`/`atan2`, so results need not match any particular authored triple numerically — only the resulting orientation. At the gimbal-lock poses (Y at ±90°) the X and Z angles are ambiguous; this decomposition resolves them by convention with Z set to zero. Used by angular rotation tracks (§9.1) when authored angles are not available.

**Returns**

- `readonly [number, number, number]`

# RenderTarget
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/rendertarget/

<Signature
  code="interface RenderTarget {
	dispose?(): void;
	setTransform(matrix: Matrix4): void;
}"
/>

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/types-ts/#L27" label="types.ts:27" />

The structural render target interface (§17.1). Any object with a `setTransform` method is a valid target — custom rendering systems do not need to inherit from a library class or import anything from it.

The engine owns playback state; the target owns rendering-specific state only (§17.2). Adapters translate evaluated transforms into rendering-system-specific operations and never own animation time or playback lifecycle (§3.6). Disposing a playback must not destroy the underlying DOM element, canvas context, or graphics resource — targets are not owned resources (Appendix B.8) — so `dispose` is optional and reserved for adapter-owned bookkeeping only.

**Example**

```ts
const recorder: RenderTarget = {
  matrices: [] as Matrix4[],
  setTransform(matrix: Matrix4) {
    this.matrices.push(matrix);
  },
};
animation.attach(recorder).play();
```

#### Implemented By

- [`WebGLRenderTarget`](/keyframe-flow/docs/webglrendertarget)
- [`WebGPURenderTarget`](/keyframe-flow/docs/webgpurendertarget)

---

## Methods

<MemberHeading id="dispose" depth="3" name="dispose" sig="dispose(): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/types-ts/#L31" sourceLabel="types.ts:31" />

Optional cleanup of adapter-owned state; never destroys host resources.

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="settransform" depth="3" name="setTransform" sig="setTransform(matrix: Matrix4): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/types-ts/#L29" sourceLabel="types.ts:29" />

Receives the evaluated transform as a canonical `Matrix4` (§17.1).

**Parameters**

- `matrix` ([Matrix4](/keyframe-flow/docs/matrix4))

**Returns**

- `void`

---

# RotationMode
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/rotationmode/

<Signature code="RotationMode = 'quaternion' | 'angular'" />

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/animation/animation-ts/#L26" label="animation.ts:26" />

How rotation interpolates between keyframes (§9.1).

- `"quaternion"` (default): SLERP with shortest-path — the correct choice for orientations, but equivalent orientations never describe a revolution.
- `"angular"`: component-wise interpolation of authored Euler angles in radians, enabling full revolutions without intermediate keyframes (§9.1).

---

# Scheduler
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/scheduler/

<Signature
  code="interface Scheduler {
	cancel(handle: unknown): void;
	request(callback: (time: number) => void): unknown;
}"
/>

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/timing/scheduler-ts/#L11" label="scheduler.ts:11" />

A frame callback source (§16). One `request` schedules exactly one callback invocation — the same contract as `requestAnimationFrame` — and `cancel` aborts a request that has not fired yet. The clock and scheduler are kept separate on purpose: scheduling is not timekeeping (Appendix B.7), so the engine reads timestamps from a `Clock` rather than trusting callback arguments.

#### Implemented By

- [`ManualScheduler`](/keyframe-flow/docs/manualscheduler)

---

## Methods

<MemberHeading id="cancel" depth="3" name="cancel" sig="cancel(handle: unknown): void" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/timing/scheduler-ts/#L15" sourceLabel="scheduler.ts:15" />

Cancels a previously requested callback that has not fired yet.

**Parameters**

- `handle` (unknown)

**Returns**

- `void`

<MemberHeading id="request" depth="3" name="request" sig="request(callback: (time: number) => void): unknown" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/timing/scheduler-ts/#L13" sourceLabel="scheduler.ts:13" />

Schedules `callback` for the next frame; returns a cancelable handle.

**Parameters**

- `callback` ((time: number) => void)

**Returns**

- `unknown`

# target
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/target/

<Signature
  code="target: {
	canvas: (context: CanvasRenderingContext2DLike, options?: Canvas2DTargetOptions) => RenderTarget;
	html: (element: CssTransformElementLike, options?: HtmlTargetOptions) => RenderTarget;
	svg: (element: SvgTransformElementLike) => RenderTarget;
	webgl: (options?: WebGLRenderTargetOptions) => WebGLRenderTarget;
	webgpu: (options?: WebGPURenderTargetOptions) => WebGPURenderTarget;
}"
/>

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/index-ts/#L25" label="index.ts:25" />

Built-in render target factories (§17).

```ts
spin.attach(target.html(element)).play();
spin.attach(target.svg(gElement)).play();
spin.attach(target.canvas(ctx2d)).play();
spin.attach(target.webgl({ onTransform: uploadAndDraw })).play();
```

Custom rendering systems skip this namespace entirely: any object with a `setTransform(matrix)` method is a valid target (§17.1).

**Properties**

- `canvas` ((context: [CanvasRenderingContext2DLike](/keyframe-flow/docs/canvasrenderingcontext2dlike), options?: [Canvas2DTargetOptions](/keyframe-flow/docs/canvas2dtargetoptions)) => [RenderTarget](/keyframe-flow/docs/rendertarget)) — `canvas` — Canvas 2D CTM adapter with explicit projection (§17.3).
- `html` ((element: [CssTransformElementLike](/keyframe-flow/docs/csstransformelementlike), options?: [HtmlTargetOptions](/keyframe-flow/docs/htmltargetoptions)) => [RenderTarget](/keyframe-flow/docs/rendertarget)) — `html` — CSS `matrix3d()` transform adapter for HTML elements (§17).
- `svg` ((element: [SvgTransformElementLike](/keyframe-flow/docs/svgtransformelementlike)) => [RenderTarget](/keyframe-flow/docs/rendertarget)) — `svg` — SVG 1.1 `matrix()` transform attribute adapter (§17).
- `webgl` ((options?: [WebGLRenderTargetOptions](/keyframe-flow/docs/webglrendertargetoptions)) => [WebGLRenderTarget](/keyframe-flow/docs/webglrendertarget)) — `webgl` — column-major matrix upload adapter for WebGL hosts (§3.6).
- `webgpu` ((options?: [WebGPURenderTargetOptions](/keyframe-flow/docs/webgpurendertargetoptions)) => [WebGPURenderTarget](/keyframe-flow/docs/webgpurendertarget)) — `webgpu` — column-major matrix upload adapter for WebGPU hosts (§3.6).

---

# Transform
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/transform/

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/transform-ts/#L53" label="transform.ts:53" />

An immutable transform with the canonical component representation `{ position, rotation: Quaternion, scale }` (§4.3), available as the frozen `components` property.

Euler angles are accepted only as a construction interface in radians; rotations are stored internally as quaternions (§4.3). Every operation returns a new transform without modifying its source (§4.2).

Composition follows §4.4 exactly: fluent operations are applied in call order as local-space operations (right-multiplication, `M ← M × Op`), and parent-to-child composition uses `Parent × Local`. When a composed result cannot be represented as ordinary TRS components — for example rotation appended after non-uniform scale, which introduces shear — the operation throws explicitly rather than silently approximating (§4.3, §9.2). Use `Matrix4` directly for such matrices.

---

## Constructors

<MemberHeading id="constructor" depth="3" name="constructor" sig="new Transform(components: TransformComponentsInit): Transform" />

**Parameters**

- `components` ([TransformComponentsInit](/keyframe-flow/docs/transformcomponentsinit), default: `{}`)

**Returns**

`Transform`

---

## Properties

<MemberHeading id="components" depth="3" name="components" sig="components: Readonly<TransformComponents>" />

<MemberMeta badges="readonly" sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/transform-ts/#L55" sourceLabel="transform.ts:55" />

Canonical position/rotation/scale components; frozen and never mutated.

## Methods

<MemberHeading id="compose" depth="3" name="compose" sig="compose(local: Transform): Transform" />

<MemberMeta sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/transform-ts/#L118" sourceLabel="transform.ts:118" />

Composes `parent × local` into a new transform (§4.4). The local transform is interpreted in the parent's coordinate system. Throws when the composed matrix is not representable as TRS components.

**Parameters**

- `local` ([Transform](/keyframe-flow/docs/transform))

**Returns**

- [`Transform`](/keyframe-flow/docs/transform)

**Example**

```ts
const arm = transform().translate(100, 0); // parent
const item = transform().rotateZ(Math.PI / 2); // child in parent frame
const world = arm.compose(item); // Parent × Local (§4.4)
```


# TransformComponents
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/transformcomponents/

	scale: Vector3;

The canonical component representation of a transform (§4.3): position, quaternion rotation, and scale. Shared by the transform and matrix subsystems; declared as a pure type so neither module depends on the other at runtime.

# TransformKeyframeSource
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/transformkeyframesource/

Sources accepted for `keyframes` definitions (§5.4): arrays, synchronous iterables, generator instances, and functions returning synchronous iterables. All are consumed eagerly and exactly once when the animation definition is created (§5.5).

# Vector3
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/vector3/

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/transform/vector3-ts/#L31" label="vector3.ts:31" />

An immutable 3D vector in the library's right-handed coordinate system (§4.4).

All operations return new vectors; instances are never mutated (§4.2).

**Example**

```ts
const v = new Vector3(1, 2, 3);
const unit = v.normalize(); // (0.267, 0.535, 0.802) — new vector, `v` intact
```

---

- `z` (number, default: `0`)

# WebGLRenderTarget
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/webglrendertarget/

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/webgl-ts/#L27" label="webgl.ts:27" />

WebGL render target adapter (§3.6, §20 M5).

**Remarks**

The adapter owns only rendering state: the latest evaluated transform as a column-major `Float32Array` — the exact layout `gl.uniformMatrix4fv` and GLSL `mat4` consume (§15) — plus an optional upload callback. It creates no GL resources, never touches playback time or lifecycle (§3.6), and disposal cannot destroy contexts, buffers, or programs (Appendix B.8). Hosts draw in the `onTransform` hook or poll [WebGLRenderTarget.matrixValues](/keyframe-flow/docs/webglrendertarget#matrixvalues) from their own render loop.

---

## Properties

<MemberHeading id="ontransform" depth="3" name="onTransform" sig="onTransform: (matrix: Float32Array) => void" />

<MemberMeta badges="readonly" sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/webgl-ts/#L12" sourceLabel="webgl.ts:12" />

Upload hook invoked after every evaluation with the new column-major matrix values — typically `gl.uniformMatrix4fv(location, false, values)` plus a draw call. Returning here rather than owning a GL program keeps the adapter free of shader and pipeline assumptions (§17.2).

---

# WebGPURenderTarget
Source: https://johnsonjo4531.github.io/keyframe-flow/docs/webgpurendertarget/

<SourceLink href="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/webgpu-ts/#L28" label="webgpu.ts:28" />

WebGPU render target adapter (§3.6, §20 M5).

**Remarks**

The adapter owns only rendering state: the latest evaluated transform as a column-major `Float32Array`, matching WGSL's `mat4x4<f32>` uniform layout element-for-element (§15). It creates no GPU resources, never touches playback time or lifecycle (§3.6), and disposal cannot destroy devices, buffers, or encoders (Appendix B.8) — hosts encode work in the `onTransform` hook or read [WebGPURenderTarget.matrixValues](/keyframe-flow/docs/webgpurendertarget#matrixvalues) from their own frame loop.

---

## Properties

<MemberHeading id="ontransform" depth="3" name="onTransform" sig="onTransform: (matrix: Float32Array) => void" />

<MemberMeta badges="readonly" sourceHref="/keyframe-flow/docs/source/targets/webgpu-ts/#L13" sourceLabel="webgpu.ts:13" />

Upload hook invoked after every evaluation with the new column-major matrix values — copy them into your uniform buffer (WGSL `mat4x4<f32>` uses the same column-major layout, §15) and encode draw calls. Keeping command encoding host-side leaves device, queue, and pipeline ownership with the host (§17.2).
